correctness.rationale: For K_N every edge pair determines a unique rank-two flat; hence distinct flats meet in at most one edge. A nonstar family contains a triple A,B,C with three distinct pair-intersection edges e,f,g. Their three-edge graph has four admissible incidence types (three disjoint, exactly one meeting pair, two meeting pairs as a 4-path, or a 3-star); a three-cycle would yield duplicate flats. Enumerating every flat meeting the triple yields exactly the 3-,4-,5-member extensions. Full edge stars have size C(N-1,2) and become maximal for N>=5, while N=4 stars extend. Exact counts and boundaries follow from choosing supports. Fresh independent bitset maximal-clique enumeration: n=4 histogram {5:3}, n=5 {6:10,5:15,4:10}, n=6 {10:15,5:45,4:60,3:15}; finite checks corroborate, not prove all N.

evidence: Cao–Liao–Zhang arXiv:2608.05951 Lemma 3.6: nontrivial intersecting rank-two family has at most five members; equality pattern only.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The size-five extremal theorem constrains but does not classify smaller inclusion-maximal size-three/size-four families; the precise sizes/counts require extra case analysis.
